parole.testo: From a- + *rost + -ire, with the root being of Germanic origin; cf. Frankish *rōstjan (“to roast”), from Proto-West Germanic *raustijan (“to roast”), from Proto-Indo-European *Hrews- (“to crackle, roast”). Compare Sicilian arrùstiri, Catalan rostir, French rôtir.
From Germanic *takka; see German Zacke, Dutch takk, West Frisian tak, Middle Dutch tacke, all from Proto-West Germanic *takkō (“twig, branch, shoot”).
